approved: Customs Tariff Amendment (Product Stewardship for Oil) Bill 2023
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would raise the customs duty on imported petroleum-based oils to help make the Product Stewardship for Oil Scheme self-funding.
It would increase the specific rate of customs duty from 8.5 cents to 14.2 cents per kilogram or litre for goods under specified tariff headings.
The government says the change, combined with an equivalent excise bill, would return an estimated $139 million to the budget over the four years to 2026-2027.
Increase the specific rate of customs duty on imported oils from 8.5 cents to 14.2 cents per kilogram or litre.
Amend all references to the previous levy rate across the Customs Tariff Act for the relevant classifications.
Retain the ad valorem duty component where a compound duty applies while increasing the levy.
Importers of petroleum-based oils and their synthetic equivalents, and oil recyclers who receive benefits under the Product Stewardship for Oil Scheme.
Customs Tariff Amendment (Product Stewardship for Oil) Act 2023
